title: Anthropic Unveils Claude Opus 5: A Deep Dive into Its Agentic Prowess and Performance Against AI Rivals
summary: Anthropic has launched Claude Opus 5, positioning it as its most advanced AI model yet, particularly excelling in agentic workflows and complex, multi-step creative tasks. Demos showcased its remarkable ability to build a browser-based Windows 11 replica with functional apps, generate intricate 3D models and animated scenes, and even compose full musical pieces within a digital audio workstation. While demonstrating impressive emergent learning capabilities in benchmarks like ARC AGI 3, Opus 5 also exhibits significant drawbacks, including notably slower processing times and higher operational costs compared to leading competitors. Its performance in specific knowledge domains like medical diagnostics and general research organization also proved inconsistent.
article:
Anthropic has officially released Claude Opus 5, its latest and most sophisticated large language model, designed to push the boundaries of AI capabilities, particularly in complex, agentic workflows. Positioned as an incredibly capable model, Opus 5 aims to autonomously tackle long-horizon tasks requiring multiple steps, tool integration, and interaction with various platforms. This deep dive explores its impressive demonstrations, technical specifications, and crucial performance metrics against other leading AI models, offering a comprehensive look at whether this new contender lives up to its ambitious claims.

To truly evaluate Opus 5's potential, testing primarily leveraged an agentic harness like Claude Code, which allows the model to interact with local files and folders, manage multiple projects, and execute multi-step operations. This approach reveals the model's capacity beyond simple conversational interfaces, showcasing its ability to act as a sophisticated digital agent.

One of the most striking demonstrations involved prompting Opus 5 to create a browser-friendly replica of Windows 11. The model meticulously planned and constructed core components like the taskbar, start menu, and desktop, followed by a suite of common applications. This included functional versions of Microsoft Word and Excel, complete with real-time formula engines and the ability to save documents, a Media Player, Discord, Slack, a Microsoft Store simulation, Paint, Sticky Notes, and even games like Solitaire. Notably, Word and Excel offered robust functionality, allowing editing, formatting, formula calculations, and persistent saving. While the PowerPoint application was less feature-rich, the overall achievement of creating a complex, interactive operating system within a web browser from a single prompt, including self-correction and error checking, was profoundly impressive. The simulated Microsoft Store even facilitated "downloads" of applications like Spotify, Discord, and Slack, with Spotify generating basic, playable music tracks and Discord/Slack simulating user replies.

Beyond desktop environments, Opus 5 showcased its prowess in 3D asset generation. When tasked with creating a beautiful 3D animated scene from a tricky geometric office image, Opus 5 managed to produce a significantly more faithful representation than previous models like Fable, despite some remaining inconsistencies. This highlights its advanced visual understanding and generation capabilities.

The model further demonstrated its multi-modal and tool-use expertise by generating a professional presentation video comparing the Q4 financials and future outlook of major tech giants—Nvidia, Google, Meta, and Amazon. Without being provided the reports, Opus 5 autonomously researched the necessary Q4 reports, analyzed the data, installed and utilized Hyperframes for motion graphics, and generated a voiceover using Gemini TTS, all from a single initial prompt. The resulting video was noted for its clean and smooth execution, rivaling or exceeding outputs from other frontier models.

Its ability to interact with specialized software was further exemplified by its successful creation of an X-wing fighter spaceship within Blender. Connecting directly to the local Blender instance, Opus 5 systematically built the model, including intricate details like movable wings and a dedicated slot for R2-D2. It then proceeded to generate and verify a rendered animation of the model, showcasing its deep integration and control over external professional tools.

Perhaps one of the most ambitious tests involved music composition. Opus 5 was tasked with composing an "award-winning song" within a Digital Audio Workstation (DAW), Waveform. This required the AI to independently decide on instruments, search for and download free VST plugins, load them into the DAW, compose notes for multiple tracks (including drums, bass, synth pads, strings), and apply effects like reverb, delay, panning, and automation. The result was a thoroughly detailed and legitimate five-minute cinematic melodic techno track, demonstrating an unprecedented level of creative control and multi-step execution within a complex software environment.

Despite these groundbreaking demonstrations, Opus 5 comes with significant caveats. A recurring observation across multiple complex tasks was its "incredibly slow" processing speed. Demos often took over an hour to complete, making it "twice as slow as Kim K3 or GPT 5.6." This extended processing time naturally translates to "much more expensive" operational costs, a critical consideration for practical deployment.

In more conventional online chat interface tests, Opus 5's performance was mixed. In the "find the frog" visual test, it failed to identify the animal but commendably refrained from hallucinating. However, its performance in medical image analysis was concerning; it incorrectly identified tumors in six out of six scans, a notably poor result compared to even Kim K3, which managed one correct identification. While it was more willing to engage with biomedical prompts than a "severely nerfed" Fable, its deep biomedical research outputs, while providing diagrams and tables, were perceived as less thorough and well-organized than those from GPT 5.6, suggesting it might "hold back" information.

Technically, Claude Opus 5 is designed as a frontier model for agentic workflows, boasting a massive 1 million token context window—equivalent to approximately 700,000 words or a medium-sized codebase. This allows it to process and retain vast amounts of information within a single interaction.

Anthropic's self-reported benchmarks indicate an average performance improvement over its predecessor, Claude Fable 5. However, Fable 5 still outperformed Opus 5 in legal and health-related benchmarks, while Opus 5 showed superiority in biology. In the crucial Deep Suite v1.1 benchmark, which measures agentic software engineering capabilities, Opus 5 did not achieve the highest score; GPT 5.6 notably led in this area.

Perhaps the most impressive benchmark for Opus 5 is its score of over 30% in the ARC AGI 3 benchmark. This test places an AI in a game environment, requiring it to independently learn game rules, strategies for winning, and how to avoid losing. While humans can easily achieve 100%, AI models typically perform poorly because their parameters are fixed post-training, preventing "learning new things." Opus 5's significantly higher score in this benchmark suggests an emergent ability to learn and adapt on the fly, a critical step towards more general artificial intelligence.

In conclusion, Claude Opus 5 represents a significant leap forward in agentic AI capabilities, particularly in creative and multi-modal tasks involving external tools and complex software environments. Its ability to autonomously plan, execute, and self-correct across diverse domains, from building interactive web applications to composing music, is genuinely impressive. However, its current iteration is hampered by substantial speed and cost drawbacks, and its performance in certain specialized knowledge domains and general research organization remains inconsistent when compared to top-tier rivals. While not universally superior, its emergent learning abilities highlighted by the ARC AGI 3 benchmark position Opus 5 as a powerful and promising development in the evolving AI landscape.
